summary.text: Jennifer Wortz is a Republican state representative from Michigan House District 35 who took office on January 1, 2025, and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election. She owns and operates Central Grace Farms, a family agricultural business.

paragraphs.text: Jennifer Wortz earned a bachelor's degree in agriculture communications from Michigan State University in 2000.
Her career experience includes working as a high school Agriscience teacher, a homeschool educator, and a partner in a family-owned agricultural business.

In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey, Wortz said she grew up on a small cash crop and beef farm in Hillsdale County, that her family started Central Grace Farms in 2016, and that she works as the Branch County Conservation District Manager.
She named regulatory overreach from state government as one of the biggest issues she sees and said she wanted to create better small business growth options and decrease energy and fuel costs.
Wortz assumed office in the Michigan House on January 1, 2025, and advanced from the Republican primary on August 4, 2026.
In the 2025-2026 session she is majority vice chair of the House Agriculture Committee and also sits on the Natural Resources and Outdoor Recreation and Transportation committees.
